message:
Fermat's Last Theorem in Lean 4 (Lean 4.33.1, Mathlib v4.33.0)

A complete machine-checked proof of Fermat's Last Theorem: the import
closure of FinalCheck.lean - 1,450 definition modules (Definitions/),
29,511 statement modules (Theorems/), 29,511 proof modules (P2M/Sol/),
P2M/Util.lean, one derive module - on toolchain leanprover/lean4:v4.33.1
with Mathlib tag v4.33.0 (db584cd6d46c92f209a44c0f1c829460d327499d).
FinalCheck.lean pins '#print axioms fermat_last_theorem' to [propext,
Classical.choice, Quot.sound] and derives Mathlib's FermatLastTheorem
from it.

This is the port to Lean 4.33.1 of the proof first checked on Lean
4.30.0. Against the 4.30.0 text the only changes are the Mathlib renames
and mechanical proof repairs the newer Mathlib required (about 9,200
modules differ in text); the theorem proved, the axioms it rests on and
the structure of the argument are unchanged. Checks on exactly these
sources: the full build succeeds with the axiom list above; the comparator
(leanprover/comparator v4.33.0) accepts the solution against a challenge
file that states the theorem citing only Mathlib - statement identity,
permitted axioms, and a replay of the whole environment in the Lean kernel;
nanoda, an independent kernel implementation, accepts the same
environment. README.md gives the results and how to re-run them
(verification/comparator/run.sh, verification/nanoda/run.sh);
PROOF-PATH.md names each step of the argument and the Lean theorem that
carries it; NOTICE and ATTRIBUTION.md carry the licence and the
third-party attribution (Imperial College London FLT project,
flt-regular, Mathlib); formalization.yaml records the project
metadata.

Also included: html/, a set of static web pages presenting the proof
(open html/index.html in a browser; no server or network needed), and
tools/docs-site/, the program that generated them from the Lean sources.
